ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper left of the figure is the three-terminal voltage regulator W7812, pin 1 is connected to the input Ui, pin 3 is connected to the output terminal Uo on the right, and pin 2 goes downward as the reference terminal. On the right side, resistor R1 is connected downward from the pin 3 output node, and the lower end of R1 is then connected to the load RL to ground; beside it, the output current Io is marked as flowing downward through this branch. The pin 2 reference node of W7812 is also connected to ground through R2, and is connected to the input/feedback wiring of amplifier A; the amplifier is connected to the node at the lower end of R1 and the upper end of RL, making this node controlled to follow the potential of the regulator reference terminal. Reasoning: This circuit is a constant-current regulation structure. Under ideal conditions, W7812 keeps the voltage between pin 3 and pin 2 at 12 V. Since the amplifier makes the node at the lower end of R1 equal to the pin 2 reference potential, the voltage across R1 is 12 V. R1 is in series with the load current branch, so the output current equals the R1 current: Io = 12 V / 1 kΩ = 0.012 A = 12 mA. In the ideal calculation, R2 and RL mainly affect bias and compliance range, and do not change this constant-current value.
